THREE schoolboys were "boiled to death" after falling into a "hot sewer" used to supply heating to a Russian city. One of the eight year olds fell into the 80C-plus underground conduit - and they other two were dragged in as they tried to rescue their friend. The tragedy has stunned the city of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky after the failure to repair a hole in the sewer in the grounds of their school in the extreme east of Russia. The three were named as Daniil Slisarenko, Alexander Sanko and Daniil Viik. "A wooden decking covering the hot sewer evidently broke or collapsed leaving a two and a half metre hole," reported The Siberian Times -- http://siberiantimes.com/other/others/news/n0570-tragedy-has-three-8-year-old-boys-die-after-falling-in-boiling-sewer/ "Some reports were that it was covered in cardboard. "Locals had reported a problem at the site, but it had not been repaired. The hot water in the sewer was used for the city heating supply. " City newspaper publisher Yevgeny Sivayev, said: "It is no exaggeration to say that the city is crying. Such grief we have not had before. "It is impossible to look at children - their bodies are packed in bags." Pictures showed their remains in black bags in the snow at the site of the horror. He added: "Judging by the fact that straps of the first boy's backpack were torn off, his friends wanted to help him as he fell and pulled him up. "It did not work. So they fell in there trying to save him. "The rescuers first found them, and could not reach the first boy for a long time. "The temperature there is over 80C, very high." It is unclear why the boys were at school on 29 January because all educational institutions were supposed to be closed due to "Why they were there at all is not clear. "After all, 28 January was declared quarantine for influenza, and all schools were closed." A police source said: 'The three boys disappeared on Thursday afternoon. 'They had left the school but had not come home. 'Police, volunteers and Emergencies Ministry employees had started searching for them. 'The boys' bodies were found in the open hatch of a hot sewer located near the school building.' City mayor Dmitry Zaitsev is to pay for the funerals. A criminal probe has been launched into suspected negligence into a failure to respond to warnings from locals that the sewer was not safe.
